George Gamow was a Soviet-American theoretical physicist and cosmologist who became one of the key developers of the Big Bang theory. He made pioneering contributions to nuclear physics by explaining how radioactive decay happens through quantum tunneling, and later ventured into molecular biology, where he proposed that genetic code uses a triplet codon system.

In 1928, Gamow explained alpha decay through quantum tunneling, showing how alpha particles can escape the strong nuclear force barrier even though they lack the classical energy needed to do so. This single insight unlocked a major problem in nuclear physics.

His most famous contribution came in 1948, when he co-authored the Alpher-Bethe-Gamow paper — sometimes called the alpha-beta-gamma paper, a playful reference to the three authors' names. This paper explained the cosmic abundance of hydrogen and helium through nucleosynthesis during the early hot universe, providing the foundation for Big Bang cosmology. That same year, working with Ralph Alpher and Robert Herman, he predicted the existence of the Cosmic Microwave Background radiation, which he described as the leftover heat of the Big Bang itself.

In nuclear physics, Gamow formulated the Gamow-Teller transition, describing a specific type of beta decay in which the spins of the emitted electron and antineutrino couple to a total spin of one. Later, he pivoted to molecular biology and proposed the triplet code hypothesis — the idea that combinations of three DNA bases code for one of the twenty amino acids. He founded the RNA Tie Club to research the genetic code, an exclusive dining club for scientists working on this problem.

Gamow also wrote the popular science book series Mr Tompkins, which made relativity and quantum physics accessible by explaining them through the dreams of an ordinary bank clerk. Einstein worked on the expanding universe solutions to general relativity that formed the mathematical foundation for Gamow's Big Bang model. Gamow was a contemporary of Enrico Fermi, and both worked on beta decay and nuclear physics.
